recent_posts.title: Pretext and Donald Knuth
recent_posts.summary: Mathias Biilmann describes two typographic improvements made to his blog using Cheng Lou's new pretext JavaScript library. The first applies the Knuth-Plass text justification algorithm — a global paragraph optimization approach originally developed for TeX — to produce evenly spaced justified text, unlike the greedy line-by-line method built into browsers. The second scales article titles to fit on a single line at exactly 80% of viewport width or the full content column width. The implementation was driven by an AI agent runner using a short prompt referencing pretext's example code.

recent_posts.title: AI and Ambition
recent_posts.summary: Mathias Biilmann, CEO of Netlify, shares how AI coding agents like Claude Code enabled him to implement creative, whimsical features on his personal blog that he would never have had time for otherwise. Examples include a scroll-based reading progress animation and a dynamic magazine-style homepage that gets redesigned for each new post. The broader argument is that AI's most underappreciated value isn't efficiency — it's expanding ambition, enabling developers and builders to pursue ideas that would never make a roadmap or fit a busy schedule.

recent_posts.title: How platforms should distinguish AI agents from malicious bots
recent_posts.summary: A personal experiment with an AI agent (Openclaw) led to a Google account being disabled for bot-like behavior. The author reflects on the broader industry challenge of distinguishing legitimate personal AI agents from malicious bots. Current fraud prevention heuristics—captchas, phone verification, bot detection—treat agents the same as bots, blocking legitimate use. The author argues the industry needs to shift from detecting 'is this a bot' to detecting 'is this doing bad things,' and that platforms must build proper standards for agent identity and authentication or risk becoming irrelevant as personal agents become mainstream.

recent_posts.title: One Year of AX
recent_posts.summary: Agent Experience (AX) has evolved from a developer-focused concept to a broader discipline essential for all digital products. The framework encompasses four key areas: Access (enabling agents to use products on behalf of users), Context (managing information flow within agent loops through techniques like MCP and content negotiation), Tools (providing APIs, CLIs, and MCP servers for agent interaction), and Orchestration (triggering and managing agent workflows at scale). Initially adopted by developer tool companies, AX is expanding beyond software development as autonomous agents like Claude Code and Clawdbot demonstrate how AI will fundamentally change how users interact with products and services.

recent_posts.title: How AI agents will reshape software development in 2026
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents like Claude Code are fundamentally transforming software development, enabling non-programmers to build real applications through prompting rather than traditional coding. This shift will drive "True Computer Literacy" where writing software becomes as essential as using it. The emergence of autonomous agents will necessitate new paradigms: Agent Experience (AX) as a design discipline, faster deployment pipelines with isolated sandboxes for testing, and a move away from strict syntax toward natural language interfaces. Tools and platforms that fail to adapt to agent-driven workflows will become irrelevant as the developer population expands from 17 million to potentially 3 billion.

recent_posts.title: AI code agents expand web development from 17 million to 3 billion potential developers
recent_posts.summary: AI code agents are transforming web development by enabling anyone with basic software skills to build websites and applications. This shift expands the potential developer base from 17 million professionals to 3 billion internet users, creating new roles where non-technical professionals like marketers and product managers can leverage coding agents. The evolution requires developer tools to focus on agent experience rather than traditional developer experience to remain relevant in this changing landscape.

recent_posts.title: Why AX should mean agent experience not agentic experience
recent_posts.summary: Mathias Biilmann clarifies that AX should stand for 'Agent Experience' rather than 'Agentic Experience', arguing that agents should be treated as a new type of user with their own unique needs. He draws parallels to established concepts like User Experience (UX) and Developer Experience (DX), emphasizing that agents have both superhuman capabilities and surprising limitations that require thoughtful product design.

recent_posts.title: AI in the CLI: the Humanoid Robot of the Web
recent_posts.summary: CLI-based AI coding agents represent the digital equivalent of humanoid robots, offering generic capabilities across all computing tasks rather than specialized functions. Unlike vertical AI agents built for specific enterprise tasks, coding agents can inherently program tools, access servers, manipulate databases, and orchestrate sub-agents through the command line interface. This positions foundational model companies to naturally evolve into coding agent companies, creating truly generic agents capable of any cyberspace task that human developers can perform.

recent_posts.title: Happy WWW Launch Date!
recent_posts.summary: Celebrating the 36th anniversary of Tim Berners-Lee's World Wide Web announcement, this reflection explores how the web transformed global communication and compares it to today's AI revolution. The author argues that despite concerns about AI potentially disrupting the web through agents and LLMs, the web platform remains more relevant than ever, with increased developer adoption, faster app deployment, and the continued importance of URLs and domains in an AI-driven world.

recent_posts.title: Building a Notion publishing system using AI without writing code
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their experience building a complete Notion-to-blog publishing system using AI assistance without writing code manually. The system automatically transforms unstructured Notion documents into structured markdown blog posts, handles image processing, and creates GitHub pull requests. Built using Netlify's serverless stack (Background Functions, Blob Storage, Edge Functions), it integrates three APIs (Notion, OpenAI, GitHub) to create a seamless publishing workflow. The author reflects on how AI is changing software development, shifting focus from implementation details to architectural decisions and user experience design.
